title: Research: bound every chronological ADD error in the persistent z4 echo
body:
The PR1410/PR2464 persistent pair saves scalar gates but leaves its precision tradeoff unproved. This package reconstructs the unchanged 2016/1904-record signed words and every chronological ADD-error impulse. The joint word has forward `(Gamma,M)=(703,6945)` versus `(431,3990)` for separate calls; inverse values are `(701,5012)` versus `(429,3197)`.

With exact NEG and local ADD error `|e| <= u(|approx dst|+|approx src|)`, the proved all-cut feedback bound is `E <= B*M*u/(1-2*Gamma*u)`. The uniform sufficient fractional guard is 13 to 14 bits forward and 12 to 13 bits inverse. These are sufficient bounds in the explicit model, not minimum actual precision, physical host admission, or new kappa.

Validation: full Python 3.12.14 registered replay passed, including exact source word hashes, separately implemented reverse covector witnesses, directly attaining independent-error-box examples, five semantic controls, relocated replay and four actual corruptions. A separate AI-assisted proof read and optimized verifier replay found no actionable issue. Reproduce with `python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/z4-persistent-error-envelope`.

Canonical main remains `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision4. Final overlap covers 698 open PRs and1202 Discussion records with complete pagination. Credit Cinna Davis / PR1391 and PR1410, Aaron Wang / PR2464, and the retained frame-interface lineage. Prepared for ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0; no human review or hosted CI success claimed.
